hints.title: Table Relationships
hints.text: Join Orders with Users on seller_id and with Items on item_id to inspect the sold item's brand against the seller's favorite brand.

hints.title: Brand Mismatch Filtering
hints.text: Filter out items where item_brand matches favorite_brand.

hints.title: Unique Item Aggregation
hints.text: Group by seller_id, count distinct item_id, and filter for sellers achieving the maximum count.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH RankedSellers AS (
    SELECT 
        o.seller_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.item_id) AS num_items,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT o.item_id) DESC) AS rk
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN Users u ON o.seller_id = u.seller_id
    JOIN Items i ON o.item_id = i.item_id
    WHERE i.item_brand <> u.favorite_brand
    GROUP BY o.seller_id
)
SELECT 
    seller_id,
    num_items
FROM RankedSellers
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY seller_id ASC;
```

variables: N: total records in Orders table
complexity.notes: Hash join and distinct aggregation followed by top count filtration.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per seller lead to quadratic runtime.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for aggregation hash tables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use CTE or window ranking to handle ties at maximum count gracefully.

import pandas as pd

def market_analysis_iii(orders: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame, items: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = orders.merge(users, on='seller_id').merge(items, on='item_id')
    filtered = merged[merged['item_brand'] != merged['favorite_brand']]
    if filtered.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=['seller_id', 'num_items'])
    grouped = filtered.groupby('seller_id')['item_id'].nunique().reset_index()
    grouped.rename(columns={'item_id': 'num_items'}, inplace=True)
    max_items = grouped['num_items'].max()
    res = grouped[grouped['num_items'] == max_items].sort_values('seller_id')
    return res
